instruction: I'm reading lecture materials with VLC playing background music. The VLC interface has too many controls and buttons that I don't need while just playing audio. Could you enable the minimal view mode so the player interface is simpler and less cluttered?

parameters.window_name: lecture.pdf — 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Lecture 2: Data Structures

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to enable VLC's minimal view mode (qt-minimal-view=1). The evaluator uses existing check_qt_minimal_view metric to verify that qt-minimal-view setting is set to 1 in VLC config file.
metadata.verification: Verified using existing check_qt_minimal_view function. Expected value: qt-minimal-view=1 (enabled). Default is 0 (disabled).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement to enable VLC minimal view mode
Getter (get_vlc_config) properly reads VLC configuration file from ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc on Linux
Metric (check_qt_minimal_view) correctly searches for 'qt-minimal-view=' setting and compares against expected value
Expected value (qt-minimal-view=1) is semantically correct - 1 enables minimal view, 0 disables it (default)
Postconfig properly kills and relaunches VLC to ensure configuration is persisted to disk
Logic handles edge cases correctly - uses default '0' if setting not found in config file
Complete coverage - evaluator checks exactly what the instruction requires, nothing more or less
